html:
A performing arts centre on Sydney Harbour, designed by the Danish architect Jørn Utzon and opened in 1973. Its white shell roofs make it one of the most famous buildings of the 1900s.

Utzon won an international competition in 1957 with sketches of sail-like shells. No one yet knew how to build them. Work began in 1959, and after years of trials Utzon and the engineers at Ove Arup found a solution: every shell is cut from the same imaginary sphere, so the curved ribs could be made from standard parts.

Costs and delays grew without end. The budget of a few million dollars rose more than tenfold, paid mostly by a state lottery. In 1966, after a bitter fight with a new state government over money and design, Utzon resigned and left Australia. He never returned to see the finished building.

Queen Elizabeth II opened it in October 1973. Standing beside the Harbour Bridge, it became the symbol of Sydney and of Australia. It was made a World Heritage Site in 2007.
sum: A performing arts centre on Sydney Harbour, designed by the Danish architect Jørn Utzon and opened in 1973. Its white shell roofs make it one of the most famous buildings of the 1900s.
